recent_posts.title: Shimmer: The animated student short that reached Mexico’s biggest stage
recent_posts.summary: Shimmer (Fulgores) is an animated short film created by students at Escena, a Mexican animation school, using Unreal Engine 5. Originally planned with Arnold renderer, the team switched to UE5 mid-production to enable real-time lighting previews—critical since light is a central narrative device in the film. The switch allowed a small team without a render farm to iterate rapidly, with the director personally lighting around 50 shots. The film won Best Animated Short Film at Mexico's Ariel Awards and is Oscar-qualified, demonstrating how real-time pipelines can help educational animation teams achieve professional-level results.

recent_posts.title: Bringing stunning visuals to UE mobile games with Arm Accuracy Super Resolution
recent_posts.summary: Arm Accuracy Super Resolution (ASR) is a free UE5 plugin built on AMD FSR2 and optimized by Arm for mobile GPUs. It reduces GPU load, lowers skin temperatures, and minimizes thermal throttling on mobile devices while maintaining or improving visual quality. Fortnite's integration is highlighted as a case study: the team used ASR to re-enable previously disabled features like ambient occlusion and additional shadow cascades, resolved ghosting artifacts via a reactive mask, and achieved consistent 60Hz gameplay with lower power draw. ASR is platform-agnostic, supporting Vulkan, OpenGL ES, and DirectX 11/12 across Android and iOS.

recent_posts.title: How ZDT used Unreal Engine 5 to build a cinematic octopus platformer
recent_posts.summary: ZDT's team of gaming, animation, and VFX veterans discuss how they used Unreal Engine 5 to build Darwin's Paradox!, a cinematic 2.5D platformer starring a stealthy octopus. Key topics include using Blueprint visual scripting for rapid prototyping, UE's material system and render targets to simulate octopus camouflage, combining Maya animations with real-world dynamics for organic character movement, and designing a UI-free experience to maintain cinematic immersion. The 15-person team leveraged Blueprint for gameplay mechanics, narrative scripting, and UI, transitioning to C++ only when performance demanded it.

recent_posts.title: Free pack of 280 automotive Substrate materials now available for Unreal Engine 5.7
recent_posts.summary: A free pack of over 280 production-ready automotive Substrate materials is now available on Fab for Unreal Engine 5.7. The pack covers common vehicle material types including paints, leathers, metals, glass, plastics, emissive screens, and lighting elements. Material parameters are derived from real-world lab measurements for physical accuracy, and a Blueprint lookup tool lets teams compare metal presets. The included environment is calibrated for both Lumen and path tracing using luminance and color temperature meters, making it a reliable validation environment for automotive visualization.

recent_posts.title: UE5 is becoming the platform of choice for robotics simulation
recent_posts.summary: Unreal Engine 5 is gaining traction as a robotics simulation platform, particularly as a synthetic data factory for AI training pipelines. Synthetic data offers key advantages over manual annotation: consistent labels, no annotator disagreements, and no costly quality-control loops. Economically, synthetic data becomes more cost-effective than manual annotation after only tens of thousands of images, and with robotics models requiring millions of images, the cost savings are substantial. Market signals indicate synthetic data is on track to become a dominant component of AI training pipelines.

recent_posts.title: How Unreal Engine brought fast iteration to complex shots on ‘Sinners’
recent_posts.summary: The VFX team behind the horror film 'Sinners' used Unreal Engine as a shared real-time visualization platform to plan complex sequences, including a stitched IMAX music montage and a period-accurate train arrival. Rather than treating it as a traditional previs tool, they built interactive, playable versions of scenes early in production so all departments could align on creative intent before cameras rolled. The visualizations persisted through post-production, helping the editor shape cuts and maintain continuity of intent throughout the pipeline.

recent_posts.title: ‘Max & the Midknights’: Creating a stop-motion look with UE5
recent_posts.summary: Nickelodeon's 'Max & the Midknights' reinvented TV animation by building its entire world in Unreal Engine 5 and adopting a live-action-inspired production pipeline. Instead of starting with storyboards, the team first constructed a fully modular CG world, then used virtual cameras to shoot coverage before storyboarding only confirmed shots—eliminating waste. The show achieves a stop-motion aesthetic through techniques like animating on twos, oversized textures implying miniature models, and handcrafted VFX including cotton-string smoke and replacement-piece fire geometry. The entire season ran in a single UE5 project shared by up to 10 artists simultaneously, enabling unprecedented flexibility across all 20 episodes.

recent_posts.title: MetaHuman Creator Web Application is being Discontinued
recent_posts.summary: Epic Games is discontinuing the MetaHuman Creator (MHC) web application over the course of 2026, with full shutdown on November 5, 2026. MetaHuman creation has been fully integrated into Unreal Engine since UE 5.6. The decommissioning happens in stages: older UE version support (4.27–5.1) drops April 5, 2026; UE 5.2–5.4 support drops June 5, 2026; and UE 5.5 support ends November 5, 2026. Users have a 90-day retrieval window after the final shutdown before their MetaHumans are deleted. Existing users should export their MetaHumans via Quixel Bridge or migrate them to MHC in UE 5.6+ following the provided migration guide. MetaHumans created in UE 4.27 cannot be upgraded or migrated.

recent_posts.title: Reimagining Previs and Layout for 'KPop Demon Hunters' with Unreal Engine
recent_posts.summary: Sony Pictures Imageworks used Unreal Engine to overhaul the previs and layout pipeline for the Netflix animated film KPop Demon Hunters. The team built a workflow connecting Maya, Unreal Engine, and USD to bring animation rigs into real-time and visualize complex concert lighting and crowd scenes earlier in production. A custom plugin was developed to export animated lighting curves via USD into Foundry's Katana, preserving F-curve data without baking per-frame keys. The result was a 20–25% improvement in layout and previs efficiency, with the pipeline now serving as a foundation for future Sony Pictures Imageworks projects.

recent_posts.title: Unreal Fest Chicago 2026
recent_posts.summary: Unreal Fest Chicago 2026 takes place June 16-18 at McCormick Place Convention Center. The event features the State of Unreal keynote, technical sessions, an expo floor with Epic tools and partner demos, a Dev Hub for expert advice, and networking events. Super-early bird tickets are $549 (until Feb 16), early bird tickets are $649 (Feb 17-Mar 31), and student tickets are $499. The three-day conference includes sessions on engine features, hands-on demos of Unreal Engine, UEFN, Fab, MetaHuman Creator, and other Epic ecosystem tools.

top_posts.title: No Captain Allowed! is a co-op game developed by a two-person team
top_posts.summary: No Captain Allowed! is a co-op game developed by a two-person team 9heads. The game was developed by Daniel Ernesto and Henrique Elias, who graduated together in Game Design in 2010. It was released on Steam at the end of 2012. The game includes a procedural map that randomizes different elements.
